"executive_summary": "This note addresses the problem of finding a geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of the open modular curve Y0(p) over Q, where Y0(p) is X0(p) with its two cusps removed. The background is Mazur's theorem that the Shimura covering X2(p) → X0(p) of degree Np = (p−1)/gcd(p−1,12) is the maximal unramified abelian covering of the whole curve X0(p). The gap is that X0(p) is proper, so its two cusps are ramification points; removing them enlarges the pool of available unramified coverings. The authors prove that the maximal unramified abelian covering of Y0(p) is cyclic of degree 2Np, obtained by adjoining a square root of an explicitly constructed rational function Fh^2 on X2(p). The construction uses generalized Dedekind eta functions (Siegel functions) Eg, whose transformation and cusp-order properties are recalled and applied. The key result is that Fh^2 is a modular function on X2(p) defined over Q whose order at every cusp is odd, so that X'2(p) → X2(p) is a degree-two cover ramified exactly at the cusps, and the composite X'2(p) → X0(p) is geometrically maximal unramified over Y0(p). The proof splits into the case p ≢ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) is a genuine intermediate group) and the case p ≡ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) = Γ1(p) and a triplet construction is used). The note is theoretical, with no numerical experiments, datasets, or code. The main quantitative facts are the degree 2Np, the index [Γ0(p):Γ2(p)] = k = Np, the index [Γ2(p):Γ1(p)] = ℓ = gcd(p−1,12)/2, and the order-2 character machinery. The theoretical implication is that the maximal unramified abelian extension over Y0(p) is a quadratic extension of the Shimura field, controlled by the coinvariants of the generalized Jacobian's torsion.",

summary.title: Maximal abelian extension of a modular curve unramified outside cusps
summary.field_subfield: Number theory / arithmetic geometry (modular curves, abelian extensions)
summary.type_of_paper: Short research note / proof of a theorem
summary.executive_summary: This note addresses the problem of finding a geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of the open modular curve Y0(p) over Q, where Y0(p) is X0(p) with its two cusps removed. The background is Mazur's theorem that the Shimura covering X2(p) → X0(p) of degree Np = (p−1)/gcd(p−1,12) is the maximal unramified abelian covering of the whole curve X0(p). The gap is that X0(p) is proper, so its two cusps are ramification points; removing them enlarges the pool of available unramified coverings. The authors prove that the maximal unramified abelian covering of Y0(p) is cyclic of degree 2Np, obtained by adjoining a square root of an explicitly constructed rational function Fh^2 on X2(p). The construction uses generalized Dedekind eta functions (Siegel functions) Eg, whose transformation and cusp-order properties are recalled and applied. The key result is that Fh^2 is a modular function on X2(p) defined over Q whose order at every cusp is odd, so that X'2(p) → X2(p) is a degree-two cover ramified exactly at the cusps, and the composite X'2(p) → X0(p) is geometrically maximal unramified over Y0(p). The proof splits into the case p ≢ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) is a genuine intermediate group) and the case p ≡ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) = Γ1(p) and a triplet construction is used). The note is theoretical, with no numerical experiments, datasets, or code. The main quantitative facts are the degree 2Np, the index [Γ0(p):Γ2(p)] = k = Np, the index [Γ2(p):Γ1(p)] = ℓ = gcd(p−1,12)/2, and the order-2 character machinery. The theoretical implication is that the maximal unramified abelian extension over Y0(p) is a quadratic extension of the Shimura field, controlled by the coinvariants of the generalized Jacobian's torsion.

claims.description: The maximal unramified abelian covering of Y0(p) over Q is cyclic of degree 2Np, a quadratic extension of the Shimura cover.
Generalized Dedekind eta functions (Siegel functions) produce explicit modular functions whose cusp orders are odd.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This note addresses the problem of finding a geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of the open modular curve Y0(p) over Q, where Y0(p) is X0(p) with its two cusps removed. The background is Mazur's theorem that the Shimura covering X2(p) → X0(p) of degree Np = (p−1)/gcd(p−1,12) is the maximal unramified abelian covering of the whole curve X0(p). The gap is that X0(p) is proper, so its two cusps are ramification points; removing them enlarges the pool of available unramified coverings. The authors prove that the maximal unramified abelian covering of Y0(p) is cyclic of degree 2Np, obtained by adjoining a square root of an explicitly constructed rational function Fh^2 on X2(p). The construction uses generalized Dedekind eta functions (Siegel functions) Eg, whose transformation and cusp-order properties are recalled and applied. The key result is that Fh^2 is a modular function on X2(p) defined over Q whose order at every cusp is odd, so that X'2(p) → X2(p) is a degree-two cover ramified exactly at the cusps, and the composite X'2(p) → X0(p) is geometrically maximal unramified over Y0(p). The proof splits into the case p ≢ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) is a genuine intermediate group) and the case p ≡ 11 mod 12 (where Γ2(p) = Γ1(p) and a triplet construction is used). The note is theoretical, with no numerical experiments, datasets, or code. The main quantitative facts are the degree 2Np, the index [Γ0(p):Γ2(p)] = k = Np, the index [Γ2(p):Γ1(p)] = ℓ = gcd(p−1,12)/2, and the order-2 character machinery. The theoretical implication is that the maximal unramified abelian extension over Y0(p) is a quadratic extension of the Shimura field, controlled by the coinvariants of the generalized Jacobian's torsion.

Research Context
The setting is the maximal unramified abelian covering of a curve over a number field. The relevant group is the maximal abelian quotient of the étale fundamental group. The geometric part is the kernel of the map to the absolute Galois group. This geometric part is finite, which guarantees a maximal covering exists. Mazur's theorem establishes the maximal unramified covering of X0(p) as the Shimura cover. The Shimura covering has degree Np = (p−1)/gcd(p−1,12). The gap is that X0(p) is proper, so its cusps are ramification points. Removing the cusps enlarges the set of available unramified coverings.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is the degree of the maximal unramified abelian covering of Y0(p). The hypothesis is that this covering is a cyclic quadratic extension of the Shimura cover. The predicted outcome is that the degree is exactly 2Np, twice the Shimura degree. The predicted structure is a factorization through X2(p) via a degree-two cover. The predicted ramification is exactly at the cusps. The predicted field generator is a square root of an explicit rational function. The predicted tool is generalized Dedekind eta functions. The predicted modular-function property is that Fh^2 has odd order at each cusp.

Methodological Details
The base field is Q and the curves are X0(p) and X1(p) over Q. The base curve Y0(p) is X0(p) with its two cusps 0 and ∞ removed. The analysis requires X to admit a degree one divisor. The generalized Jacobian is defined in the sense of Rosenlicht–Serre. The generalized Jacobian is a semi-abelian variety fitting an exact sequence. The torsion module is defined via Hom from the Tate module to Q/Z(1). The character group LD has rank rD = Σ[x∈D][k(x):k] − 1. The abelian fundamental group is identified with Hom(MµTor(−1), Q/Z). The covering invariants Σ(f) and ΣD(f) are kernels of pull-back maps. The maximal unramified Galois groups are Hom(Σ, Q/Z(1)). Geometric maximality is defined by Σ(f) = JµTor. A maximal covering exists when k is finitely generated over its prime subfield. The prime p is assumed odd, and the main case is p ≥ 5. The construction splits into the case p ≢ 11 mod 12 and p ≡ 11 mod 12. The second case uses Γ2(p) = Γ1(p) and a triplet of integers. The second author's funding is from Taiwan's Ministry of Science and Technology.

Procedures And Architectures
The generalized Dedekind eta function Eg is defined via an infinite product. The Bernoulli polynomial used is B(x) = x^2 − x + 1/6. These functions are also called Siegel functions up to scalars. The transformation Eg+N = E−g = −Eg is a key property. The transformation under Γ0(N) is given by explicit root-of-unity factors. Products of Eg form modular functions on Γ1(N) under congruence conditions. The conditions require Σeg ≡ 0 mod 12, Σgeg ≡ 0 mod 2, Σg^2 eg ≡ 0 mod 2N. The function Fh is a 6th-power root of a product of ℓ eta functions. The indices are k = Np = (p−1)/gcd(p−1,12) and ℓ = gcd(p−1,12)/2. The group Γ2(p) is generated by Γ1(p) and a matrix with g^k in the top-left. The indices satisfy [Γ0(p):Γ2(p)] = k and [Γ2(p):Γ1(p)] = ℓ. Fh^2 is a modular function on X2(p) defined over Q. The field Q(X'2(p)) is a quadratic extension of Q(X2(p)). The extension is generated by a square root of Fh^2. The character ψ is the order-2 character of SL(2,Z) with explicit values. The character χ is the order-2 character of Γ2(p) when ℓ is even. The group Γ'2(p) is the kernel of ψχ or ψ, and Γ0(p)/Γ'2(p) is cyclic of order 2k. The covering X'2(p) → X2(p) ramifies exactly at each cusp.

Key Results
The main theorem states the maximal covering of Y0(p) is cyclic of degree 2Np. The covering factors as fp ∘ πp with πp of degree two. The restriction to Y0(p) is geometrically maximal unramified. The order of MµTor(−1) is either Np or 2Np. The degree-2Np cover automatically satisfies the maximality condition. The generalized eta function Eg satisfies Eg+N = E−g = −Eg. The functions Fh satisfy Fh = F−h = Fp+h. The sign of Fgkh depends on p mod 4. Fh^2 is a modular function on X2(p) defined over Q. The order of Fh^2 at any cusp of X2(p) is odd. The epsilon factor to the sixth power equals ψ(γ). The sum Σ_{j=0}^{ℓ−1} g^{2jk} is ≡ 0 mod p since ℓ > 1. The factor 2p divides S, giving Fh(γτ) = ψ(γ)Fah(τ). The order of Fh^2 at a non-cusp p∤c cusp is 1. The order of Fh^2 at a p|c cusp is odd via a floor-function computation. The congruence reduces to p ≡ 1 mod 2 for the p|c cusps. The field Q is algebraically closed in Q(X'2(p)). The function z(τ) = (η(τ)/η(pτ))^(12/(p−1,12)) is also modular on Γ'2(p). The relation between Fh and z is a product over j. The group Γ'2(p) is normal in Γ0(p) with quotient cyclic of order 2k. For p ≢ 1 mod 8, z transforms by ψ under Γ2(p).

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The maximal unramified abelian covering of Y0(p) is a quadratic extension of the Shimura field. The doubling reflects the Z/2Z coinvariants of the generalized Jacobian. The odd cusp orders force ramification exactly at the cusps. The construction realizes the abstract maximal covering concretely. The result extends Mazur's theorem to the cuspidally-open curve. The degree-two cover is unramified outside cusps. The theory links generalized Jacobians to unramified coverings. The eta-function approach provides explicit generators.

Contradictions And Limitations
The case p ≡ 11 mod 12 requires a separate construction. The case p = 2 or 3 is handled trivially via Gm. The existence of a maximal covering needs k finitely generated over its prime subfield. The proof is non-canonical in the splitting of the exact sequence.

Claims
The maximal unramified abelian covering of Y0(p) over Q is cyclic of degree 2Np, a quadratic extension of the Shimura cover. The main theorem asserts degree 2Np. The covering factors through X2(p) via a degree-two map. The order of MµTor(−1) is Np or 2Np. The degree-2Np cover satisfies the maximality condition.  
Generalized Dedekind eta functions (Siegel functions) produce explicit modular functions whose cusp orders are odd. The eta product Eg+N = E−g = −Eg. The construction requires p ≥ 5. The case p ≡ 11 mod 12 needs a different construction. Odd cusp orders force ramification exactly at cusps. The field is generated by a square root of Fh^2. The eta approach gives explicit generators.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The proof is split by the case p ≢ 11 mod 12 versus p ≡ 11 mod 12. The case p = 2 or 3 is handled via Gm. The odd case ℓ > 1 uses the vanishing sum mod p. The even case uses the character χ of order 2.

Key Figures Tables
The paper contains no figures or tables.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is proving the maximal unramified abelian covering of Y0(p) is cyclic of degree 2Np. 2. The strongest evidence is the odd cusp order of Fh^2 forcing ramification exactly at the cusps. 3. The future path is extending this to other modular curves and level structures.
